invariants: Repository identity is independent of hosting URL, provider, default branch and associated product.
A fork or independently governed mirror receives a distinct repository identity and records provenance to its source.
Hosting migration changes locators and bindings without rewriting repository or source-revision identity.
Immutable source revisions are content-addressed or otherwise cryptographically pinned and never replaced in place.
Mutable branch and tag references are aliases and never suffice as reproducible build inputs without a resolved revision.
Each build input records the exact repository revision used at execution time.
Repository access policy never grants product, runtime or deployment authority by implication.
Repository records never contain credentials, private keys or reversible secret representations.
Software Product, Component, Build, Release, Artifact and Deployment remain externally mastered and separately identified.
Archival and retirement preserve revision resolution, provenance and tombstone history.
One product may reference multiple repositories and one repository may support multiple products without identity merging.
Retired repository identifiers are never recycled.
